stemMd: A drawer contains 5 black, 7 white and 9 grey socks. Socks are drawn without looking. What is the minimum number needed to guarantee at least three socks of the same colour?
explanationMd: To avoid three of any colour, draw at most two from each of the three colours, for six socks. A seventh must belong to one of those colours and raises its count to at least three. This worst-case argument proves the minimum guarantee.

distractorRationale.a: The first three could have three different colours.
distractorRationale.b: A distribution of two, two and one avoids three of one colour.
distractorRationale.c: Two socks of each colour still avoids three of one colour.
distractorRationale.e: Seven already guarantees the required repetition.
